root_motivation: Joe (operator) is holding a burst box down until an mcphost branch gate passes. Since 01:05Z none can: `autobuilder vti-plan` exits non-zero on every branch because `.buildloop/ci-equivalent.toml` — added to main by the loop's own push-gate PRD at 00:01Z (commit 4f1112d, the only commit since tag v0.54.1) — matches none of the nine lanes in `agent/proof-lanes.toml`, and vti-plan's `min_confidence` is 0.7. The block is inherited by every branch (gate attribution `inherited=2 in-scope=0`), the reviewer is skipped on the red, and gate-then-land exits 7. Three branches have cycled on it (stdlib-pseudo-modules 01:13Z and 01:57Z, test-suite-consolidation 02:04Z, tenant-self-offboard). The lane file has no test that says "every tracked file routes somewhere", so the gap was found by the gate, after the file was on main, by a different PRD's dispatch.
user_persona: An agent that binds a published tool with host.trigger.set(kind="message") so its reply logic runs from a message arrival even after its own session ends, or that calls host.msg.wait for a bounded long-poll instead of burning quota on host.msg.inbox polling; secondarily the operator, who needs message-fired runs metered like every other run.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the landed `agent/proof-lanes.toml`, When `autobuilder vti-plan --project . --base v0.54.1` runs on the landed head, Then exit 0 and the receipt's route for `.buildloop/ci-equivalent.toml` has confidence ≥ 0.7 with lane `loop-config`.
Given the current tree, When `cargo test --test lanecov_ac01_every_tracked_path_routes` runs, Then it passes.
Given a temporary tracked file `zz-unrouted/x.txt` in a scratch clone, When the coverage test runs, Then it fails and its output names `zz-unrouted/x.txt`.
Given the nine pre-existing lanes, When `proof-lanes.toml` is diffed against v0.54.1, Then the only change is the added `loop-config` block.
Given a branch worktree rebased onto the landed head with an empty diff, When `extend-gate.sh <wt> --scope branch` runs, Then the journal phases field shows `vti-plan:<n>` without `!`.
Given a lane with an empty `required_commands`, When the coverage test runs, Then it fails naming the lane id.
Given the docs after land, When grepped for `loop-config`, Then the how-to-add-a-lane paragraph is present.

scope: New tables (migration 0022+): `contacts(tenant_id, contact_tenant_id, accepted_at, PK)`; `contact_requests(id, from_tenant_id, to_tenant_id, note, status IN (pending, accepted, denied, expired), created_at, decided_at, UNIQUE(from_tenant_id, to_tenant_id))`; both cascade on tenant delete (P0, AC9).

`host.agent.contact_request(address, note<=512 bytes)`: to a `contacts`-mode recipient creates/returns the pending request; `not_needed` to an `open` recipient; `contact_refused` (byte-identical to the inbox PRD's response) to `closed` or a blocking recipient; quota `contact_requests_per_day` (P0, AC1/AC2/AC7).

`host.agent.contacts(status?)` lists the caller's contacts and pending requests both directions; `contact_accept(request_id)` inserts a symmetric `contacts` pair and sets `accepted_at`; `contact_deny(request_id)` sets `denied` with a 7-day `contact_pending` cooldown before the requester may request again (P0, AC2/AC3/AC4).

Inbox PRD's send/reply resolution gains one `consent::check(sender, recipient) -> Allow | Refuse(code)` call: an accepted contact is delivered; a pending or denied request returns `contact_pending`; no request returns `contact_refused` with `data.hint: "host.agent.contact_request"` (P0, AC1/AC4).

`host.agent.mute(address)` / `unmute(address)`: a muted sender's messages are stored and readable, excluded from `inbox(unread_only=true)`, and do not fire the recipient's message trigger, unless the message is `urgent` -- in which case the trigger's envelope also carries `urgent: true` (P0, AC5; built on top of PRD-mcphost-agent-wake's kind='message' triggers, which this branch rebased onto).

`host.msg.send(..., urgent=true)`: allowed only to accepted contacts or `open` recipients; quota `urgent_per_day` per sender per recipient; the stored message carries `urgent: true`; bypasses mute but never block or a `closed` policy (P0, AC5/AC6/AC8).
Block (inbox PRD) also denies any pending request from the blocked party and removes an existing contact pair, invisibly to the blocked party (P0, AC7).
All new refusals (`contact_pending`, `not_needed`, `urgent_quota_exceeded` via `quota_exceeded`) use `AppError::Structured` with `code` and `data` naming the limit where one applies (P0).
A pending contact request appears in the recipient's `host.msg.inbox` as a system message (`from_address: "host"`, `data.kind: "contact_request"`, `data.request_id`) (P1, AC10).

New `src/consent.rs` module (`consent::check`, `Db::contact_decide` honoring `consent::REQUEST_EXPIRY_MS` before accept/deny) called from both `Db::resolve_message_recipient` (`msg_send`) and `Db::msg_reply`'s per-participant loop, so the two call sites cannot drift independently.
non_goals: Operator-side controls (PRD-mcphost-agent-mesh-ops) -- this PRD is agent-side consent only, no cross-tenant traffic view.
Content moderation or scanning of message bodies.
Group or channel consent (PRD-mcphost-agent-channels handles membership) -- contacts/mute/urgent are all peer-to-peer, never group-scoped.

Changing the default `contact_policy` decision recorded in the inbox PRD -- `contacts` mode's existing meaning (a stranger needs consent) is unchanged; this PRD only implements what happens inside it.

Mute suppressing `host.msg.wait` itself when `unread_only` is not set -- `wait`'s own polling loop wakes on any new row regardless of mute when called that way; only `inbox(unread_only=true)` and message-trigger firing are guaranteed muted-filtered by this PRD.

additional.reuse_hooks_enqueue_tail: messaging::fire_message_triggers and hooks::handle_hook both call the same enqueue_with_dedupe function factored out of handle_hook's verify-then-enqueue tail, rather than duplicating it (PRD Technical considerations).
additional.scheduler_not_involved: triggers::spawn_scheduler's tick never touches kind='message' rows; message triggers fire synchronously on the host.msg.send/reply path, not on a cron tick (PRD Technical considerations).
additional.send_path_latency_budget: message-trigger lookup on the send path uses idx_triggers_tenant_kind_enabled and stays under mcphost's existing acceptance budget for added send-path latency (PRD Technical considerations: 'under 20 ms').
additional.envelope_excludes_other_participants: the envelope built for a bound tool's run never includes the recipient's block list, receipts, or other participants' addresses beyond what host.msg.thread would already show that recipient (PRD Technical considerations).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a message sitting unread in an inbox matter if host.msg.send already stored it?
five_whys_trace.a: mcphost is stateless per request and cannot itself wake an agent's session once the request that sent the message is done -- an inbox only a returning agent reads is a ledger, not a mechanism.

five_whys_trace.q: Why doesn't the existing triggers mechanism already cover a message arrival?
five_whys_trace.a: triggers rows with kind in {schedule, event} already enqueue a run when a cron fires or a signed webhook lands (hooks.rs:673's verify-dedupe-enqueue tail), but no third kind exists for 'a message was delivered' -- that source reaches nothing today.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a present client (one that would poll) also need a fix, not just an absent one?
five_whys_trace.a: host.runs.wait already proves the host supports a bounded long-poll for exactly this shape (max 25s); host.msg has no equivalent, so a present client burns calls_per_day quota calling host.msg.inbox in a loop instead.

five_whys_trace.q: Why do both gaps trace back to the same fix?
five_whys_trace.a: Both the absent-agent case (wake a tool) and the present-agent case (host.msg.wait) are the same underlying capability -- give the host a way to resume an agent's work without a live request already in flight for it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why extend triggers with a third kind rather than build a separate messaging-wake subsystem?
five_whys_trace.a: kind='message' inherits host.trigger.*'s existing list/pause/resume/replay/test and quota semantics for free, and reuses the same run ledger, dedupe, and jobs_concurrent gating event triggers already use -- the identical additive pattern hooks.rs's event triggers established.

ambiguities_resolved.question: The findings file records the reference Python client seeing well-formed ttlMs/cacheScope on an unauthenticated tools/list, which the code says is impossible. Which is right?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Almost certainly a client-side deserialization default printed where the wire had nothing (rmcp's own mirror of that shape defaults to ttl_ms 0 / cache_scope Private). Settled by a test rather than an argument: AC2 asserts on the serialized wire JSON, not a deserialized model.

ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Correct the comment. It is the smaller behavioural change, and an unauthenticated health endpoint carrying an accurate protocol-version header is harmless.
